shreya: Heads-up — after yesterday's change to the continuous batcher (windowing + adaptive fill), we saw p95 latency regress for mixed short/long workloads. Kicked off a perf trace: http://perf.redwood/trace/18625abc

aj: Saw the same on our staging job. Short sequences that used to finish in ~12ms are now spiking to ~40-60ms. Long requests seem mostly OK.

noah: Is this the kernel-selection tweak that prefers fused-attn for >1024 seq? Could be a scheduling imbalance where long requests steal the mini-batch window.

shreya: It's the windowing change + token-budget cap per-batch. We increased window duration to 12ms to boost throughput for long tails. Hypothesis: small requests wait longer because batch doesn't flush until window or token cap reached. Also seeing tenant contention where noisy tenants flood queue with many short requests.

eva: Quick data from perf-bot: p50 unchanged, p95 +120% on short sequences, throughput similar. Flamegraph attached by perf-bot.

perf-bot: auto-report: trace=18625abc; p50=14ms; p95=58ms; median kernel time unchanged; queue-wait increased by ~35ms for 80th-95th percentile.

aj: Two orthogonal levers: (1) age-based flush (flush if oldest request > X ms), (2) per-tenant soft token budget so single tenant can't consume batch capacity. Thoughts?

noah: Agree. Also consider "min-batch evacuation" for short sequences: if a batch contains >N short requests, rotate priority and flush earlier. Could tag requests by expected token-length (heuristic from prompt length + model profile).

shreya: Nice. We can use prefix-length heuristic from routing metadata + KV cache hit hint to classify "short" vs "long". KV cache hits tend to be long chats — but sometimes short completions hit KV too. Need low-overhead.

eva: Another option: token-slice cap per-tenant per-window. Example: 50 token-slice max per tenant per 12ms window; leftover capacity can be rebalanced. That prevents tenant X from occupying entire mini-batch budget.

aj: Implementation risk: if we enforce strict per-tenant slice, we might underfill batches on low utilization and hurt throughput. So make it soft (weights) and allow unused tokens to spillover.

noah: Actionable experiment proposal:
- A: implement age-based flush at 6ms + window=12ms baseline (control: current 12ms no-age-flush)
- B: soft tenant token-slice (start 30% cap) with spillover enabled
- C: short-request early-evac rule: if >4 short requests queued, flush early
Measure: p50/p95 short-only, long-only, mixed; throughput; kernel utilization; KV hit distribution.

shreya: I'll own A and C (batcher change). aj can own B (tenant-slice). noah can do analysis dashboard updates + trace correlation.

aj: Noted. Also saw a perf regression tied to commit abcdef1 that changed queue-priority. I'll revert that in a branch and compare. Might be compounding.

eva: FYI there's a CPU path regression on CPU-backed small model runners — logs in #eng-infra. Could be orthogonal but flagging.

ops-bot: deploy queued: batcher/age-flush-experiment -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:30Z by shreya

shreya: I'll push a small instrumentation change to tag requests with "estimated-tokens" so we don't have to call full estimator in the hot path. Keep it tiny.

noah: For observability: add counters for "age-flush count", "tenant-slice-used", and track per-tenant median queue-wait. We need to show fairness improvement.

aj: If experiments look good, rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback if short p95 > baseline + 10ms.

shreya: Cool. I'll post results in 24h. Short-term snapshot: disable the kernel-selection preference for fused-attn on staging (noah) to isolate.

eva: Thanks all. Small note: remember to check KV cache TTLs — if we start flushing more often we might lose warm prefixes and increase compute. Monitor KV hit rate.

shreya: Good call. Adding KV-hit-rate to the metrics list.

aj: TL;DR: Age-based early flush + soft tenant token caps + short-evac rule. Instrument heavily. Owner: shreya/aj/noah.

shreya: @here assigning follow-ups in linear ticket. Will link after deploy. :rocket:
